chunks.title: IEEE Robotics and Automation Society — Overview
chunks.heading: What IEEE RAS is
chunks.text:
The IEEE Robotics and Automation Society (IEEE RAS) is IEEE's global professional society for robotics and automation. Its mission is to "foster the development and facilitate the exchange of scientific and technological knowledge in Robotics and Automation that benefits members, the profession and humanity."

Its vision is to "be the most recognized and respected global organization in Robotics and Automation."

chunks.title: IEEE Robotics and Automation Society — Overview
chunks.heading: Field of interest
chunks.text:
On the robotics side, RAS covers robotic systems that use sensors and actuators to operate autonomously or semi-autonomously, often in cooperation with humans, with an emphasis on intelligence and the ability to adapt to the environment.

On the automation side, RAS focuses on the efficiency, productivity, quality and reliability of autonomous systems, particularly those working in structured environments such as factories.

chunks.title: IEEE Robotics and Automation Society — Overview
chunks.heading: History
chunks.text:
- 1984: the Robotics and Automation Council (RAC) was founded under the leadership of George Saridis. Eight existing IEEE societies, including the Control Systems Society and the Computer Society, came together to form it.
- 1985: the IEEE Journal of Robotics and Automation began publishing.
- 1987: the council became a full IEEE Society, the IEEE Robotics and Automation Society.
- 1988: the first IEEE/RSJ IROS conference was held at the Tokyo University of Science, Japan.
- 1989: the journal was renamed IEEE Transactions on Robotics and Automation.
- 2004: the journal split, and its robotics side continued as IEEE Transactions on Robotics (T-RO).
- June 1, 2015: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L) launched.
- 2026: ICRA was held in Vienna, Austria. ICRA 2027 will be held in Seoul, Republic of Korea.

Size and reach:
RAS has over 19,000 members around the world. It has more than 220 local and student branch chapters across IEEE's regions, with members in more than 40 countries, and 47 technical committees.

chunks.title: IEEE Robotics and Automation Society — Overview
chunks.heading: Leadership
chunks.text:
The IEEE RAS Executive Committee lists Nancy Amato (University of Illinois Urbana) as President and Kyu-Jin Cho (Seoul National University) as President-Elect. The Junior Past President is Aude Billard (EPFL), and the Senior Past President is Frank Park (Seoul National University).

RAS is governed by an Executive Committee and an Administrative Committee (AdCom), with boards for conferences, publications, educational activities, technical activities and member activities.

chunks.title: IEEE Robotics and Automation Society — Overview
chunks.heading: What RAS does
chunks.text: RAS publishes journals and magazines, runs and sponsors conferences worldwide, connects members through technical committees and chapters, runs education programmes, recognises achievement through awards, and develops IEEE standards for robotics.

chunks.title: IEEE RAS Publications and Journals
chunks.heading: Overview of RAS journals
chunks.text: IEEE RAS publishes and co-sponsors ten journals and magazines. Titles published by RAS: T-RO, RA-L, T-ASE, RA-M, RA-P, T-FR and the newer T-SRO. Co-sponsored titles: T-RL, ToH and T-MRB. RAS members get online access to key titles such as RA-M, T-RO, T-ASE and RA-L, plus discounted subscription rates.

chunks.title: IEEE RAS Publications and Journals
chunks.heading: T-RO — IEEE Transactions on Robotics
chunks.text: T-RO publishes research papers that represent major advances in the state of the art in all areas of robotics, combining theory, design, experiments, algorithms and applications. Its ieee-ras.org page lists a JCR Impact Factor of 11.1 (2025), and open-access publication is available. It traces back to the IEEE Journal of Robotics and Automation (1985), which became IEEE Transactions on Robotics and Automation in 1989 and IEEE Transactions on Robotics in 2004.

chunks.title: IEEE RAS Publications and Journals
chunks.heading: RA-L — IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
chunks.text:
RA-L launched on June 1, 2015. It is an electronic-only journal built for rapid publication: papers are six pages, with up to two extra pages allowed at a charge, and most papers get a decision within 6 months. Accepted RA-L papers can be presented at ICRA, IROS or CASE within 270 days of acceptance.

T-ASE — IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering:
T-ASE covers automation science and engineering. It is the Society's main journal for automation research.

chunks.title: IEEE RAS Publications and Journals
chunks.heading: RA-M — IEEE Robotics and Automation Magazine
chunks.text: RA-M is the Society's flagship magazine, published quarterly in March, June, September and December. It presents high-impact research articles in an engaging, accessible style, along with reviews, columns and opinion pieces, and bridges academic journals and industry publications. Website: ramagazine.ieee.org.

chunks.title: IEEE RAS Publications and Journals
chunks.heading: RA-P — IEEE Robotics and Automation Practice
chunks.text:
RA-P launched in December 2024. It publishes applied research from practitioners with real-world deployments, in a short format: up to four pages, plus one page for supplementary materials and one page for references (4+1+1).

T-FR — IEEE Transactions on Field Robotics:
T-FR is dedicated to field robotics, meaning robots working outside controlled environments. Its paper archive is freely accessible (open access) on IEEE Xplore.

chunks.title: IEEE RAS Publications and Journals
chunks.heading: T-SRO — IEEE Transactions on Soft Robotics
chunks.text: T-SRO is a newer RAS journal publishing fundamental advances in soft robotics, covering robotic systems with structural compliance: materials, sensors, actuators, design, control and AI-driven approaches. It uses double-anonymous review, and accepted papers may be presented at RoboSoft.

chunks.title: IEEE RAS Publications and Journals
chunks.heading: Co-sponsored journals
chunks.text:
- T-RL (IEEE Transactions on Robot Learning) covers fundamental advances in AI methods that address challenges specific to robotic and automation systems, including transfer learning, safe AI-based control, human-robot collaboration and reproducible benchmarks.
- ToH (IEEE Transactions on Haptics) covers haptic systems and touch feedback.
- T-MRB (IEEE Transactions on Medical Robotics and Bionics) covers medical robotics and bionics research.

chunks.title: IEEE RAS Conferences — ICRA, IROS, CASE and more
chunks.heading: ICRA — International Conference on Robotics and Automation
chunks.text:
ICRA is the IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation, the flagship conference fully sponsored by IEEE RAS. It brings together researchers and companies for paper sessions, panels, tutorials, workshops and exhibits.

ICRA 2026 was held from June 1 to June 5, 2026 at VIECON, the Vienna Congress and Convention Center in Vienna, Austria.

chunks.title: IEEE RAS Conferences — ICRA, IROS, CASE and more
chunks.heading: ICRA — International Conference on Robotics and Automation
chunks.text: ICRA 2027 will be held in Seoul, Republic of Korea, from May 24 to May 28, 2027. Paper submissions opened on July 15, 2026 and the paper submission deadline was September 15, 2026. Workshop and tutorial pre-proposals were due September 1, 2026, with full proposals due November 1, 2026. Acceptance notifications are expected on January 31, 2027 and final papers are due March 6, 2027.

chunks.title: IEEE RAS Conferences — ICRA, IROS, CASE and more
chunks.heading: IROS — International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems
chunks.text: IROS is the IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems. RAS financially co-sponsors it, and it ranks alongside ICRA as one of the premier robotics conferences. It has been held every year since 1988, when the first IROS took place at the Tokyo University of Science in Japan. Recent and upcoming hosts: 2023 Detroit (USA), 2024 Abu Dhabi (UAE), 2025 Hangzhou (China), 2026 Pittsburgh (USA), 2027 Florence (Italy).

chunks.title: IEEE RAS Conferences — ICRA, IROS, CASE and more
chunks.heading: CASE — Conference on Automation Science and Engineering
chunks.text: CASE is the IEEE International Conference on Automation Science and Engineering, the fully sponsored RAS flagship conference for automation. CASE 2026, the 22nd edition, was held in Shenyang, China, in August 2026.

chunks.title: IEEE RAS Conferences — ICRA, IROS, CASE and more
chunks.heading: Other fully sponsored RAS conferences
chunks.text:
Besides ICRA and CASE, RAS fully sponsors:
- Humanoids (IEEE-RAS International Conference on Humanoid Robots). The 2026 event is the 25th edition.
- RoboSoft (IEEE International Conference on Soft Robotics). RoboSoft 2026 was hosted in Kanazawa, Japan.
- HAPTICS (IEEE Haptics Symposium) and WHC (IEEE World Haptics Conference).
- SSRR (Safety, Security and Rescue Robotics).
- ICAR (Advanced Robotics).
- ARSO (Advanced Robotics and its Social Impacts).
- MRS (Multi-Robot and Multi-Agent Systems).
- CBS (Cyborg and Bionic Systems).
- ERAS (Engineering Reliable Autonomous Systems).

Other fully sponsored RAS conferences:
RAS also financially co-sponsors and technically co-sponsors many more conferences and workshops around the world.

chunks.title: IEEE RAS Technical Committees
chunks.heading: What technical committees are
chunks.text: IEEE RAS Technical Committees (TCs) are specialised research communities that track technical developments and encourage innovation in specific areas of robotics and automation. RAS currently lists 47 technical committees, and new ones are added as topics grow.

chunks.title: IEEE RAS Technical Committees
chunks.heading: Clusters
chunks.text:
The committees are organised into five clusters:

- Robotics Foundation Cluster
- Automation Cluster
- Human-Centered and Lifelike Robotics Cluster
- Field Robotics Cluster
- Health and Medical Robotics Cluster

chunks.title: IEEE RAS Technical Committees
chunks.heading: Recognised committees
chunks.text:
Gold Ribbon TCs include Haptics, Humanoid Robotics, Multi-Robot Systems and Soft Robotics.

Blue Ribbon TCs include Aerial Robotics and Unmanned Aerial Vehicles, Agricultural Robotics and Automation, Computer and Robot Vision, Optimization for Robotics, and Robot Control.

Joining technical committees is a benefit of RAS membership and a way to collaborate with researchers working on the same sub-field.

chunks.title: Joining IEEE RAS — Membership Benefits
chunks.heading: Membership benefits
chunks.text:
IEEE RAS membership benefits include:

- Online access to IEEE Robotics and Automation Magazine, IEEE Transactions on Robotics (T-RO), IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering (T-ASE) and IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L).
- Access to the IEEE Xplore digital library and the RAS Digital Conference Library.
- The RAS Resource Center, with conference videos and expert lectures.
- Membership in local chapters, which operate in over 40 countries.
- Participation in more than 40 technical committees.
- Discounts and an industry conference calendar covering ICRA, CASE and IROS.

chunks.title: Joining IEEE RAS — Membership Benefits
chunks.heading: How to join
chunks.text: You join RAS through IEEE. The official "Join the Robotics and Automation Society" link on ieee-ras.org leads to the IEEE membership catalog entry for RAS (product MEMRA024), which is used for both joining and renewing. General IEEE membership is available at ieee.org/join.

chunks.title: Joining IEEE RAS — Membership Benefits
chunks.heading: Students
chunks.text: The RAS Student Activities Committee (SAC) organises activities for student members, especially at RAS conferences, such as student social gatherings and team competitions. Students can also get involved through their university's RAS student branch chapter, or start one through IEEE's petition process.

chunks.title: About RAS CORE — How This Agent Works
chunks.heading: What RAS CORE is
chunks.text: RAS CORE is an autonomous retrieval-augmented AI agent. It answers questions and completes small research tasks about the global IEEE Robotics and Automation Society (its history, journals, conferences, technical committees, awards, education programmes, chapters, standards and membership), using only a curated knowledge base of publicly available information, and it cites the passages it used.

chunks.title: About RAS CORE — How This Agent Works
chunks.heading: The agent loop
chunks.text: RAS CORE runs a plan, act, observe loop on top of Gemini function calling. For every request the model decides which tool to use next, reads the result, and repeats (up to six rounds) until it has enough evidence. Only then does it write the final answer. Every step is shown live in the Agent Trace panel.

chunks.title: About RAS CORE — How This Agent Works
chunks.heading: The five tools
chunks.text:
1. search_knowledge_base: hybrid search that combines dense semantic search (cosine similarity on 768-dimensional Gemini embeddings) with BM25 keyword search, merged by Reciprocal Rank Fusion. The agent can call it several times with different queries, for example once per item when comparing two things.
2. get_document: reads every section of one document, for broad "tell me everything" questions.
3. list_topics: lists every document the agent knows about.
4. get_current_datetime: returns today's date and time in India (IST).
5. days_between: counts the days between two dates, for deadlines and countdowns.

chunks.title: About RAS CORE — How This Agent Works
chunks.heading: Grounding and citations
chunks.text: The final answer may use only facts from tool results, and the passages the agent used are listed under each answer. If the knowledge base does not contain the answer, the agent says so instead of guessing.

chunks.title: About RAS CORE — How This Agent Works
chunks.heading: The 3D constellation
chunks.text: Every glowing node in the background is one chunk of the knowledge base. Positions come from projecting the embeddings to 3D with principal component analysis (PCA), so passages with similar meaning sit close together. Each time the agent searches, a query node appears and beams connect it to the passages it retrieved.

chunks.title: IEEE RAS Awards and Recognition
chunks.heading: Society awards
chunks.text: IEEE RAS recognises outstanding work through Society awards, publication awards and conference awards. Its Society awards include:

chunks.title: IEEE RAS Awards and Recognition
chunks.heading: Society awards
chunks.text:
- Pioneer in Robotics and Automation Award: pioneering contributions to the field.
- George Saridis Leadership Award in Robotics and Automation: exceptional leadership. It is named after George Saridis, who led the founding of the Robotics and Automation Council in 1984.
- Early Academic Career Award in Robotics and Automation: early-career academics advancing the field.
- Early Government or Industry Career Award in Robotics and Automation: early-career professionals in government or industry.
- Distinguished Service Award: significant service to IEEE RAS.
- Distinguished Student Leadership Award: outstanding student leadership.

chunks.title: IEEE RAS Awards and Recognition
chunks.heading: Innovation and paper awards
chunks.text:
- ICRA Most Influential Paper Award: ICRA papers with exceptional, lasting impact.
- Inaba Technical Award for Innovation Leading to Production: technical innovations that reached the market.
- IEEE Robotics and Automation Award for Product Innovation: innovative robotics and automation products.
- IEEE/IFR Innovation and Entrepreneurship Award (IERA): innovation and entrepreneurship in robotics.

chunks.title: IEEE RAS Awards and Recognition
chunks.heading: Community awards
chunks.text:
- Most Active Technical Committee Award: the most active RAS technical committee.
- Section Chapter of the Year Award and Student Branch Chapter of the Year Award: outstanding local and student chapters.

chunks.title: IEEE RAS Education Programmes and Chapters
chunks.heading: Distinguished Lecturer Program
chunks.text: The RAS Distinguished Lecturer Program lets IEEE sections, student branch chapters and other organisations invite renowned robotics experts to speak. RAS provides travel support of up to 5,000 USD for the lecturer, with priority for chapters that have not received funding before. Distinguished Lecturers are nominated by technical committees and serve three-year terms, which helps chapters without regular access to international speakers.

chunks.title: IEEE RAS Education Programmes and Chapters
chunks.heading: Other education programmes
chunks.text: The RAS Educational Activities Board oversees summer schools, competitions, pre-college resources, technical education programmes, RAS University learning resources, CEMRA and ICRA-X. It also develops new initiatives for pre-university education and engagement.

chunks.title: IEEE RAS Education Programmes and Chapters
chunks.heading: Chapters worldwide
chunks.text:
RAS has more than 220 local and regional chapters across IEEE's regions. Chapters sponsor or co-sponsor mini-symposia, student competitions and continuing-education workshops, which is especially valuable for engineers with few robotics colleagues nearby. Local chapters operate within IEEE sections; student branch chapters are affiliated with university IEEE student branches and have a faculty advisor. New chapters are formed through IEEE's petition process.

Chapter funding:
- Chapter Start-Up Grant: 500 USD.
- Chapter Initiative Grant: up to 2,000 USD.
- Chapter of the Year awards recognise outstanding section chapters and student branch chapters.

chunks.title: IEEE Robotics Standards from RAS
chunks.heading: RAS Standing Committee for Standards
chunks.text:
The IEEE RAS Standing Committee for Standards develops IEEE standards for robotics and automation. Its published standards include:

- IEEE 1872-2015: Standard Ontologies for Robotics and Automation.
- IEEE 1873-2015: Standard for Robot Map Data Representation for Navigation.
- IEEE 1872.2-2021: Standard for Autonomous Robotics (AuR) Ontology.
- IEEE 7007-2021: Ontological Standard for Ethically Driven Robotics and Automation Systems.

These standards give robots and robotics software a shared vocabulary for knowledge, maps, autonomy and ethics, so systems from different developers can work together.
